Params: Atlantic Ocean, Earth\nRound Table Hall, Xoth Choir
Blindfolded, you are led through checkpoint after checkpoint before you finally reach the inner sanctum.
Inside the empty chamber, there is no sign of the tense standoff you were expecting.
There is only a wide, classic round table, two chairs, and an antique phonograph.
This is... a collector's edition phonograph made by the Copperfield family during the Golden Age.
It looks a lot like the one my grandpa had. I looked into it before. They were never sold to the public, only used internally as commemorative pieces.
This is my first time seeing one in person. It's even more exquisite than I imagined!
Staring at the pristine phonograph, Karenina twitches with anticipation. She wants nothing more than to lift the cover and examine its inner workings.
The moment the phonograph speaks, Karenina yanks her hand back.
That's right, it's me. I'm the Choir Administrator.
My apologies for greeting you in this form. Please, don't be alarmed.
It's hard not to be alarmed when you're talking through a phonograph!
Rest assured, I'm still human in the world outside the script.
But as the Administrator, I've chosen to present myself in this form to better convey the will of the Great One.
"Outside the script," "Administrator"... It seems that the character before you has significant authority here, far beyond what a simple NPC would possess.
It appears that "Lord Kiki" did submit the Songstress application without your knowledge.
Everything checks out. You two are free to leave Xoth immediately.
Shouldn't it be the three of us? If the misunderstanding's cleared up, Kiki—
Kiki has blasphemed our faith. The Choir exists to serve the Great One.
Everything we do, including the Songstress Trial, serves to awaken the Great One.
To deny this would shake the very foundation of the Xoth civilization.
You get a sinking feeling in the pit of your stomach.
You suddenly realize things have spiraled beyond the script.
That kind of fanatical, extremist devotion couldn't possibly come from just a screenplay.
The Corrupted prowling outside, the Choir members, and this bizarre Songstress competition... Something outside the framework of Xoth must have happened to create the current narrative.
Karenina turns to you with a questioning look almost at the same moment.
Without any idea on what kind of punishment exists in this unknown world, all you can do now is play along until you find a way out.
I want to understand the Great One.
Heavy curtains part one by one, revealing the ocean beyond the room.
Behold, this is the Great One we serve... Carcosa.
"The Great Old One", "Spawn of Azathoth", "The Unspeakable One", "The Lord of Interstellar Spaces"...
As the Administrator recites the countless titles, violent winds rise from nowhere, and dark clouds gather overhead.
A colossal shape begins to take form on the ocean's surface. Storm clouds pile high, and lightning flickers like dew.
The view from the window is no longer static. A mysterious force drags it closer to the ocean's surface, and the more you try to pull away, the deeper you're drawn in.
Even without any frame of reference, one thing is clear—it is a corpse, drifting mindlessly through the depths.
The lance embedded in its back is what killed it.
You have seen something like this before. You rack your brain, searching desperately, but the answer slips away just as it's about to surface.
Perhaps you're more familiar with another title. The mortals call the Great One... The King in Yellow.
Your Sanity bleeds away, and chaos rushes in to fill the void. Memories locked behind mental floodgates come bursting forth.
The Copperfield family... The aquarium... The Lovecraftian prototype... Carcosa...
You have seen an identical bionic creature before on the display wall at the aquarium.
The bionic construct modeled after a mythological creature is coming to life through this scripted narrative. From this moment on, the virtual world is merging with reality.
When you look up again and see the truth beneath the illusion, terror crashes down on you like a waterfall, flooding over you and coursing through every inch of your body.
Compared to the rest of you here, I know better than anyone how the ignorant masses view Carcosa.
Our Great One is far more than just some projected character in a roleplaying script.
The atmosphere in the room thickens to a standstill, and no one can predict what will happen next. All you can do is hope that things don't take a turn for the worse.
When the Punishing Virus from the surface leaked into the base, Xoth became a living hell.
We sent out many distress signals... Save me... Save us...
But who answered our cries for help...?
Neither gods nor kin... Humanity has always faced its struggles alone.
The past unfolds in the room around you. The images flash by in rapid succession, revealing what transpired scene after scene.
In the end, all we received was a blueprint for the Central Purification Filter. Oh, and it was a broadcast message.
Reading that mail, Karenina recognizes the signature at the bottom.
The sender was Cosmos Industries—now the Cosmos Technicians Union.
Week three. Three weeks after the Punishing Virus outbreak.
Want to know how we survived?
Neither of you can answer the Administrator's question. There is no comparing one person's suffering to another's.
I fled Xoth too, eventually, trying to survive out there in the world.
Until one day, I "sent away" my last companion, and I came back here instead of following the others to another conservation area.
I didn't want to be the blind old fool holding everyone back, and I didn't want to wake up one day to find I'd been left behind.
At the time, I was planning to end it all. But I wanted to come back here one last time and "see" once again before I did.
The Xoth Project did recruit a lot of blind volunteers back then.
No need to apologize. Kind souls always feel sorry for others' misfortunes, but everyone suffers in this world.
Anyway, the day I came back and slipped into this place... I saw the Great One's blessings with these blind eyes.
In an empty city, a CPF rises among the dead beside a sleeping machine.
Xoth's central mainframe was the last Corrupted here. I believe you already know its divine name.
The hero dies by the weapon they forged. The emperor falls to the kingdom they built.
There is nothing new under the sun. The same story endlessly repeats in different forms.
That's impossible. Even out there, building a CPF is a massive undertaking.
The whole process probably took longer than we thought. According to the logs, the machines never gave up resisting.
Even abandoned by their creators, they kept up their long, relentless struggle.
Karenina can't bring herself to argue further. Dismissing all this based on her experience alone would be too arrogant.
The world moves forward on trust, not suspicion. That is her belief.
Driven by the code that compelled them to protect humanity, the machines found a third option when they were faced with life or death.
Shangri-La, the Peach Blossom Spring, the Pure Land... people have always loved to describe their paradises with these fantasies.
But Xoth is a paradise I've seen with my own eyes, and it has saved me twice.
From that moment on, I decided to become a believer of Carcosa.
I have and will dedicate the rest of my life to awakening it. And of all the methods I've tried, only the <color=#FF0000>Song of True Love</color> has proven effective.
Karenina finally understands the Choir's true agenda: they worship the Corrupted as a god, weaving fiction to bring it back to life.
She stops talking and raises her weapon instead. Where reason cannot reach, force will.
Every past Songstress Trial was nothing more than a farce orchestrated by the delirious.
This situation isn't straightforward. Attack recklessly, and you may be setting off a bomb you know nothing about.
The Choir has been entrenched here for years. They must have contingencies in place.
I have witnessed the Great One's grandeur.
But where does this plan lead?
The Administrator shows no emotional reaction upon hearing your "pious" response, and she maintains her measured tone.

To bring about a new world, Carcosa descended from the distant reaches of space to Earth, and will one day return with its kin in tow. <color=#FF0000>This base follows the narrative from that myth.</color>
Xoth has been a binary structure from the very beginning... There is a mirrored installation of this underwater base in outer space.
Karenina leans in close, her voice dropping to a whisper only you can hear.
Hold on... What mythology is this even from? I never heard about this stuff during training.
Hmph. As long as it's not something weird, I guess.
Meanwhile, the Administrator continues her sermon.
Xoth, destined to be destroyed in reality, was saved by Carcosa from the script. And thus, a new fate was born.
And now, we will follow the scenario's original setup as we are led once more by the Great One of this world toward the true paradise in the mythos.
Gazing at the distant stars, you wonder if there truly exists another celestial body out there called Xoth.
Faith manifests differently among believers. The faithful call it destiny, while the skeptics call it delusion.
Karenina taps the table, trying to block out any more of this nonsense. She's clearly reaching her limit.
Look, I get where you're coming from, but that's your script.
In my script, I've got plenty of work left to do. And if I ever want to go to space or the moon or whatever, I'll get there myself.
But, my friend, this concerns you very much. Or rather... <color=#FF0000>the Songstress.</color>
But what do we gain from waking it?
Rather than asking what you stand to gain, perhaps you should consider what you stand to lose.
Another image materializes in midair. Trapped in a cell, Kiki clutches her throat, unable to make a sound.
Hah. Anyone who forces a friend's hand by threatening the friend's companion isn't what I'd call a friend.
When the day comes to awaken Carcosa, I will personally guide you there.
You shall become the new captain on the ship bound for the new world.
Hey, I'm already a captain... Forget it!
Karenina doesn't argue any further. The "person" before her can no longer distinguish reality from fantasy. Any resistance will only invite more trouble.
If I sign this, you'll release Kiki right away as promised, right? Safe and sound?
Of course. I swear it on my faith.
Karenina takes the quill pen, hesitating slightly. The "ink" dripping from it is vital fluid, but there is no wound when she opens her palm.
Her time as an Engineering Force captain has taught her that anything requiring a signature demands extra caution.
The Songstress Contract requires two signatures: yours and your "lover's."
The word "lover" hits like a torpedo plunging into the depths, and the once-solemn atmosphere explodes into a farce.
...Wait, wait, wait, what did you just say?
What is that?! Why didn't you mention that before?! This is straight-up fraud!
L-listen, the commandant isn't... We're not...
No problem. I can do it.
B-but... I still... I don't think we can... Isn't there some other way?
You... Fine... I guess it's not like I can't... But... Never mind...
Karenina ducks her head in a panic, rubbing her forehead furiously as if that might somehow hide the blush spreading across her cheeks.
You grab Karenina's hand as she signs, steadying her trembling pen.
You have seemingly eased her burden, but a searing pain shoots through your arm with each stroke of the pen.
You both sign your names: "Karenina & 【kuroname】". The instant the contract is complete, the parchment bursts into flames.
Only after you have left that gloomy mansion behind does Karenina finally let her emotions pour out.
Dammit, dammit, DAMMIT! I can't take this anymore! I seriously can't take it!
Carcosa this, Xoth that, Songstress whatever! What the hell is any of this supposed to mean?!
Karenina slumps over a table, burying her head in her arms and shaking it vigorously, seemingly trying to shake out all the nonsense she has heard today. Every last bit of it.
As much as she would like to blow off steam, she can't just fall apart when a member of her team is already down in the dumps. She has to pull it together.
Look, what's done is done. Standing around whining about it won't help. We need to focus on getting ourselves out of this mess.
No matter what, I'm not gonna sit around here like some puppet and let them pull my strings.
Like a captain surveying her fleet, Karenina casts her irritation aside, slams the table, and stands up.
Starting now, you, me, and the commandant are going to be working together on this.
Three days until the Songstress Trial
Three days until the Songstress Trial
"I'd like to live with you, in a small town, sharing endless twilights and chimes."
"In the village inn, an old clock ticks, sounding the trickle of time."
"Sometimes, at sundown: a flute in the attic, a flautist by the blind,"
"Tulips outside the windows. And if you don't love me still, I think I wouldn't mind."
The mermaid plays a folk song from the north on her moon lute, singing about polar nights, strong spirits, and freedom.
Her voice is ethereal and hauntingly beautiful, yet no passerby stops to listen. The mermaid doesn't mind, wandering as she pleases, and letting her hair tangle with the seaweed.
So many coins rest at the bottom of the pool. So many wishes people keep to themselves.
According to last night's plan, Karenina and you will keep preparing for the Songstress Trial to avoid drawing the Choir's attention, while Kiki secretly works on an escape plan from Xoth.
To prepare you two for the trial, the Choir has sent you two a list of tasks that was delivered through retinal projection.
Every time you open your eyes, floating text appears in the bottom right of your vision.
Obtain an instrument from the mermaid (0/1)\nTime Remaining: 12:34:56
Staring at the ticking timer and the to-do list, you can scarcely focus on anything else.
So Karenina drags you to the mermaid fountain in the early morning to complete the first task on the list.
The Control Court better not find out about this tech, I'm just saying.
Last thing I need is waking up to some "Unauthorized Detonation" counter every morning.
At least that will improve the safety factor...
You sit side by side with Karenina at the roadside as hibiscus petals rain down like a curtain, bathing everything in a tide of whiskey-gold.
How fast do petals fall to the ground?
A petal lands on her nose. You reach out to brush it away, only to find your hand grasping nothing.
Mm... Congrats, you just found a bug in the projection!
You laugh at her joke. Only now does the falseness of this world truly sink in.
Petals fall at five centimeters per second, but this rain of flowers will stay with you until your very last day.
Commandant, if... I mean, hypothetically, if we ever finish all our missions one day, what would you want to do?
There will always be new missions.
I don't dare imagine that day.
Hmph, fine, don't tell me then. It's not like I was that curious anyway.
Mm... If you won't tell me, I won't tell you either. That's only fair.
Whatever... I'll just tell you my plan. Maybe it'll give you some ideas!
My answer is... do nothing, think about nothing, and plan for nothing.
Karenina's voice sounds soft and fuzzy, like a small critter.
I'll head out whenever I feel like it, go see movies that just come out... Oh, and try all the ice cream flavors!
Shop at thrift stores. Listen to vinyl records. Flip them over and play them again!
I mean, I can do all that on my own... but I guess it won't be that bad if you happen to tag along!
Just so we're clear, this isn't a formal proposal! I was just... y'know, casually talking!
With that, she returns to her seat with a smile, only turning to look at you after a while.
Hey, why are you so quiet? You're laughing at how pathetic I am, aren't you?!
I shouldn't have told you in the first place.
Just as you are about to ask Karenina out on this future date, the mermaid finishes her song, and Karenina seizes the opportunity to rush over.
Looks like she's done! Hurry up and get over here, Commandant!
Next time. Next time, you will be the one who speaks up first.
The mermaid's seemingly beautiful exterior reveals the truth when you get up close. Most of her body is already rotten, scales falling from her tail. Meanwhile, a noxious stench hangs in the air.
The mermaid stands around five to six meters tall, confined within a prison centered on the fountain. She looks up and studies Karenina.
Not used to being looked at like this, Karenina instinctively crosses her arms over her chest.
So you're the new Songstress? You're quite small, aren't you?
...Hey! What're you trying to say?! Take a good look! This is the perfect height!
Hmm... you have an impressive presence that far exceeds your stature. Your projection is strong enough to handle the higher registers, and you have quite an excellent dynamic range.
Now then, what instrument should I pick for you?
How am I supposed to sing if I'm playing that thing the whole time?!
Yes! That one! That will work! And please stop recommending more weird options.
The mermaid shakes her head helplessly. Suddenly, Karenina's anchor materializes in her hands out of thin air, and when Karenina snatches the weapon back, it becomes a guitar instead.
Karenina turns it over in disbelief. Plucking a few strings to test the sound, she finds herself holding a real, playable guitar.
This is amazing, but... how does it turn back?
The magic only lasts until the performance ends.
Now, you two... here comes the price.
Nothing in Xoth is free, not even a heart this true.
The mermaid produces a goblet from thin air, filling it with liquid scooped from the pool's depths and setting it before the two of you. The liquid is murky, its contents unidentifiable.
One of you must drink this goblet of mermaid tears, then answer my question.
As for which one of you... that's entirely random.
Before you can react, the mermaid flings the contents of her goblet into the air with a flourish, and the liquid transforms into half a rainbow.
You instinctively move to shield Karenina, only to realize she has already fallen into an altered state.
Jumbled information pierces into Karenina's M.I.N.D. like corrupted data. Cold and disoriented, she has an urge to jump and scream. She doesn't just feel distressed, but also out of control.
Whoa... This is weird. Feels like something just exploded in my head.
Why do I feel so dizzy?! My legs are wobbly too.
She's fine. No one in Xoth has ever died from getting drunk.
A world without alcohol would be so dull, wouldn't it? Now, time for me to have some fun.
Come closer, my bewildered Songstress. Lend me your ear.
Tell me... do you like the human standing before you?
You don't have to answer her.
Hic... What even is liking someone anyway... Does wanting to be together count?
I feel... safe with the commandant... but it's different from the safety I feel with anyone else. Ugh, no good... I'm still so dizzy.
What about you, then? Why do you play that moon lute? Your song... it was so sad.
You are not sure if Karenina's question crosses a line. Best to apologize on behalf of your inebriated companion and give the mermaid an out.
You don't have to answer that.
It's fine. This lute was a gift from my former lover. Just like you two, we also auditioned for the role of Songstress.
After we failed, we continued to live here, pretending it never happened.
We were too ordinary, so much so that we couldn't survive without each other. Not out there in the world, and not here either.
But a person can only pretend for so long. In many moments when my heart ached, I came to understand my own feelings. I might be ordinary, but my love wasn't.

Meanwhile, Karenina is trying to climb over the railing to fish coins and the moon's reflection out of the water, and you follow her to keep her safe. But even if no one's listening, the mermaid continues her story.
So many times I wanted to ask him... but I never did. We kept losing our jobs, and things couldn't get any worse.
Until one day he told me: "I found work, Aria. Our lives are going to get better now."
Two people were selected for that position—me and him. But there was only one job.
I don't know if he knew, but among the things he brought home... was a knife.
In the end, someone got that job and survived.
You never asked him? Even at the end?
The mermaid doesn't answer. She just continues her song.
Remembering the combat knife engraved with Aria's name, you take it out and leave it by the pool before carrying Karenina away.
